Adding Environmental Covariates to MERMAID Data

Source: vignettes/articles/covariates_data.Rmd
covariates_data.Rmd

Prior to mermaidr version 2.0.0, you had the option to access environmental covariates along with data from MERMAID Collect directly in mermaidr. These covariates have been centralized into the MERMAID covariates platform, and the ability to access them has been moved to a dedicated package, mermaidrcovariates, and removed from mermaidr.

The newly released MERMAID covariates platform is a centralized, regularly updated catalogue of remote-sensing datasets — climate, environmental, and social — which are normalized so they can be paired directly with MERMAID survey locations. You can browse the full catalogue at mermaid.prescient.earth, and access the data programmatically through mermaidrcovariates, a companion to mermaidr, used throughout this vignette.

For full usage details of mermaidrcovariates, please visit its website.

This vignette will specifically walk through accessing the environmental covariates that were previously included alongside data accessed from mermaidr. Note that not all datasets were migrated:

source Data mermaidr column(s) Prescient source Prescient dataset ID
Allen Coral Atlas
Geomorphic zonation aca_geomorphic ACA Reef Extent aca_extent
Benthic habitat aca_benthic ACA Benthic Habitat aca_benthic
A global map of human pressures on tropical coral reefs by Andrello et al., 2022
Market gravity andrello_grav_nc Market gravity (fishing pressure) market_gravity
Water pollution (sediments and nitrogen) andrello_sediment, andrello_nutrient — —
Coastal population andrello_pop_count Human population within 5km (coastal population) human_pop_5km
Industrial development (number of ports) andrello_num_ports Number of ports within 5m (industrial development) num_ports_5km
Tourism (reef value) andrello_reef_value Tourism index tourism_index
Cumulative pressure index andrello_cumul_score — —
Risk-sensitive planning for conserving coral reefs under rapid climate change by Beyer et al., 2018. Scores beyer_score, beyer_scorecn, beyer_scorecy, beyer_scorepfc, beyer_scoreth, beyer_scoretr — —

We first need to access ecological data from MERMAID to link our environmental covariates to. We can link them directly to survey sites, using their latitude and longitude:

library(mermaidr)
library(tidyverse)
library(mermaidrcovariates)
library(mermaidr)
library(tidyverse)

sites <- mermaid_get_sites(limit = 2000) %>%
  filter(country == "Belize") %>%
  distinct(name, latitude, longitude)

sites
#> # A tibble: 12 × 3
#>    name          latitude longitude
#>    <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl>
#>  1 BCMR 06           18.2     -87.8
#>  2 BCMR 07           18.2     -87.8
#>  3 BCMR 22           18.1     -87.8
#>  4 BCMR 24           18.1     -87.8
#>  5 BCMR 29           18.1     -87.9
#>  6 BCMR 33           18.1     -87.9
#>  7 BCMR BR 19        18.1     -87.8
#>  8 AGGRA CAYMAN      16.0     -88.3
#>  9 BCMR 31           18.1     -87.8
#> 10 BCMR 39           18.1     -87.9
#> 11 BCMR 46           18.1     -87.9
#> 12 BCMR - Alleys     18.2     -87.8

The Allen Coral Atlas covariates (Reef Extent and Benthic Habitat) are in a raster format, while the Andrello et al. covariates contain vector data. We use different functions to access each.

Again, the mermaidrcovariates package website contains more information on the differences between these types, and how to determine if you are accessing raster or vector data.

Raster data

To access raster covariates, we use get_zonal_statistics(). We will request all data within 100 metres of each site, and then spatially aggregate that data using the mean.

Using Reef Extent as an example, the function returns the sites along with a column, zonal_statistics, that we can unnest to look at the data within:

library(mermaidrcovariates)

reef_extent <- get_zonal_statistics(sites, "aca_extent", spatial_stats = "mean", radius = 100)

reef_extent
#> # A tibble: 12 × 4
#>    name          latitude longitude zonal_statistics
#>    <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl> <list>          
#>  1 BCMR 06           18.2     -87.8 <tibble [1 × 5]>
#>  2 BCMR 07           18.2     -87.8 <tibble [1 × 5]>
#>  3 BCMR 22           18.1     -87.8 <tibble [1 × 5]>
#>  4 BCMR 24           18.1     -87.8 <tibble [1 × 5]>
#>  5 BCMR 29           18.1     -87.9 <tibble [1 × 5]>
#>  6 BCMR 33           18.1     -87.9 <tibble [1 × 5]>
#>  7 BCMR BR 19        18.1     -87.8 <tibble [1 × 5]>

reef_extent <- reef_extent %>%

In order to combine this with all of the other environmental covariates, we plan to keep the site information along with the covariate ID and value, converting it into a wide format so that, eventually, there is a column for each covariate.

reef_extent %>%
  mutate(covariate_id = "aca_extent") %>%
  select(name, latitude, longitude, covariate_id, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = covariate_id, values_from = value)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 4
#>    name          latitude longitude aca_extent
#>    <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl>
#>  1 BCMR 06           18.2     -87.8          1
#>  2 BCMR 07           18.2     -87.8          1
#>  3 BCMR 22           18.1     -87.8          1
#>  4 BCMR 24           18.1     -87.8          1
#>  5 BCMR 29           18.1     -87.9          1
#>  6 BCMR 33           18.1     -87.9          1
#>  7 BCMR BR 19        18.1     -87.8          1
#>  8 AGGRA CAYMAN      16.0     -88.3         NA
#>  9 BCMR 31           18.1     -87.8         NA
#> 10 BCMR 39           18.1     -87.9          1
#> 11 BCMR 46           18.1     -87.9          1
#> 12 BCMR - Alleys     18.2     -87.8          1

In order to not repeat the same code for each covariate, we write a helper function that gets the zonal statistics for each of the Allen Coral Atlas covariates, keeps the relevant columns, combines them, then converts into a wide format:

attach_all_raster_covariates <- function(sites, covariate_ids) {
  covariate_res <- map(
    covariate_ids,
    function(covariate_id) {
      get_zonal_statistics(sites, covariate_id, spatial_stats = "mean", radius = 100) %>%
        unnest(zonal_statistics) %>%
        mutate(covariate_id = covariate_id) %>%
        select(name, latitude, longitude, covariate_id, value)
    }
  )

  covariate_res %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = covariate_id, values_from = value)
}

raster_covariates <- sites %>%
  attach_all_raster_covariates(c("aca_extent", "aca_benthic"))

raster_covariates

Vector data

Next, we repeat a similar process for the vector covariates. This time, we use the mermaidrcovariates function attach_covariate_data(), using Human population within 5km (coastal population) as an example. We do not need to specify a radius or spatial aggregation method for vector data.

human_pop_5km <- attach_covariate_data(sites, "human_pop_5km")

human_pop_5km
#> # A tibble: 12 × 5
#>    name          latitude longitude pop_count pop_count_raw
#>    <chr>            <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>         <dbl>

#>  2 BCMR 07           18.2     -87.8     0.600          631.
#>  3 BCMR 22           18.1     -87.8     0.632          868.
#>  4 BCMR 24           18.1     -87.8     0.632          868.
#>  5 BCMR 29           18.1     -87.9     0.724         2070.
#>  6 BCMR 33           18.1     -87.9     0.696         1584.
#>  7 BCMR BR 19        18.1     -87.8     0.632          868.
#>  8 AGGRA CAYMAN      16.0     -88.3    NA               NA 
#>  9 BCMR 31           18.1     -87.8     0.632          868.
#> 10 BCMR 39           18.1     -87.9     0.696         1584.
#> 11 BCMR 46           18.1     -87.9     0.696         1584.
#> 12 BCMR - Alleys     18.2     -87.8     0.600          631.

This data is already unnested and is in a wide format; but in order to easily combine it with the other covariates, we will convert it into a long format, combine, and then re-widen. Again, creating a helper function for this:

attach_all_vector_covariates <- function(sites, covariate_ids) {
  covariate_res <- map(
    covariate_ids,
    function(covariate_id) {
      attach_covariate_data(sites, covariate_id) %>%
        pivot_longer(
          cols = -names(sites),
          names_to = "covariate_id",
          values_to = "value"
        )
    }
  )

  covariate_res %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = covariate_id, values_from = value)
}


vector_covariates <- sites %>%
  attach_all_vector_covariates(c("human_pop_5km", "market_gravity", "num_ports_5km", "tourism_index"))

vector_covariates

Combining covariates

Now that we have the two sets of covariates, raster_covariates and vector_covariates, we can easily combine them by joining them back onto the sites!

sites %>%
  left_join(raster_covariates, by = c("name", "latitude", "longitude")) %>%
  left_join(vector_covariates, by = c("name", "latitude", "longitude"))

Deprecation behaviour in mermaidr

The covariates argument in mermaid_get_project_sites() and mermaid_get_project_data() in mermaidr will now produce a message if you set it to TRUE, and returns the data without the covariates.

options(dplyr.width = 80)

p <- mermaid_get_my_projects(limit = 1)
mermaid_get_project_sites(p, covariates = TRUE)
#> ℹ `covariates` argument is deprecated as of mermaidr version 2.0.0. Please use the `mermaidrcovariates` package to access covariates. See the vignette: <https://data-mermaid.github.io/mermaidr/articles/covariates_data.html>. Your results will be returned without any covariates.
